title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases of Refusing to Execute Judgments or Rulings

articles.content_en:
Article 1 Any person with an execution obligation, such as a judgment debtor, a person with an obligation to assist in execution, or a surety, who is capable of executing a judgment or ruling of a People's Court but refuses to do so, and the circumstances are serious, shall be punished in accordance with Article 313 of the Criminal Law for the crime of refusing to execute a judgment or ruling.
For the purposes of this Interpretation, a person with an execution obligation includes natural persons and organizations.

Article 2 The "judgment or ruling of a People's Court" as provided in Article 313 of the Criminal Law refers to a judgment or ruling that is made by a People's Court according to law, has execution content, and has taken legal effect. Rulings made by a People's Court for the purpose of executing a payment order, an effective mediation document, an arbitration award, a notarized document of creditor's rights, or other similar documents in accordance with law shall be regarded as rulings under that Article.

Article 5 Being capable of execution means that the person with an execution obligation has the ability to fully or partially perform the obligation to pay property or to perform a specific act.
When determining the execution capability of a person with an execution obligation, the necessary living expenses of the person with an execution obligation and his or her dependents shall be deducted.

Article 6 Where a person, for the purpose of evading an execution obligation, commits acts such as concealing or transferring property after the commencement of litigation but before the judgment or ruling takes effect, and after the judgment or ruling takes effect, it is verified that he or she is required to execute but refuses to do so, he or she may be deemed to be capable of executing but refusing to do so, and if the circumstances are serious, criminal liability shall be investigated for the crime of refusing to execute a judgment or ruling.
The phrase "after the commencement of litigation" as referred to in the preceding paragraph generally means after the defendant receives the notice to respond from the People's Court.

Article 7 The phrase "rendering the judgment or ruling unenforceable" as provided in the Interpretation of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Article 313 of the Criminal Law and in this Interpretation generally refers to a situation where the People's Court, after taking enforcement measures in accordance with law and relevant provisions, still cannot enforce the judgment or ruling, including the situation where the judgment or ruling is entirely unenforceable or partially unenforceable.

Article 8 Where a person not a party to the case, knowing that a person with an execution obligation is capable of executing but refuses to execute a judgment or ruling of a People's Court, colludes with such person to assist in committing acts of refusing to execute, such as concealing or transferring property, thereby rendering the judgment or ruling unenforceable, such person shall be punished as an accomplice in the crime of refusing to execute a judgment or ruling.

Article 9 Where a person with an execution obligation is capable of executing but refuses to execute a judgment or ruling of a People's Court, and such act simultaneously constitutes the crime of refusing to execute a judgment or ruling, the crime of obstructing official business, the crime of assaulting police, the crime of illegally disposing of property that has been sealed up, distrained, or frozen, or any other crime, such person shall be convicted and punished in accordance with the provision that imposes a heavier punishment.

Article 10 Where a person refuses to execute a judgment or ruling regarding the payment of alimony, support, child support, pension for the disabled or survivors, medical expenses, labor remuneration, or similar payments, and the act constitutes a crime, the person shall be given a severe punishment according to law.

Article 11 Where a person commits the act of refusing to execute a judgment or ruling as provided in Article 313 of the Criminal Law, but the circumstances are obviously minor and the harm is not great, the act shall not be deemed a crime. If, before a public prosecution is instituted, the person performs all or part of the execution obligation and the criminal circumstances are minor, a decision not to prosecute may be made according to law. If, before the judgment of first instance is pronounced, the person performs all or part of the execution obligation and the criminal circumstances are minor, a lighter or mitigated punishment may be imposed, or the person may be exempted from punishment according to law.

Article 12 When a defendant is prosecuted for the crime of refusing to execute a judgment or ruling, any property that the defendant has illegally disposed of by means such as intentional damage, gratuitous transfer, transfer at a clearly unreasonable price, or false transfer shall be recovered or the defendant shall be ordered to make restitution according to law, and shall be handed over to the enforcement court for disposal according to law.

Article 13 A People's Procuratorate shall, in light of the transferred materials from investigation, review the property involved in the case, and shall put forward clear opinions on the disposition of such property when initiating a public prosecution. The People's Court shall render a judgment according to law and dispose of the property involved in the case.

Article 14 Where the applicant for enforcement has evidence to prove the existence of both of the following circumstances, and the People's Court deems that it meets the provisions of Item (3) of Article 210 of the Criminal Procedure Law, the case shall be filed and tried as a private prosecution case:
(1) the person with an execution obligation refuses to execute a judgment or ruling, infringing upon the personal or property rights of the applicant for enforcement, and criminal liability shall be investigated according to law;
(2) the applicant for enforcement has previously filed a complaint, but the public security organ or the People's Procuratorate does not investigate the criminal liability of the person with an execution obligation.
Before the judgment is pronounced, the private prosecutor may voluntarily reach a settlement with the defendant or withdraw the private prosecution.
Article 15 Criminal cases of refusing to execute a judgment or ruling shall generally be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court in the locality of the enforcement court.

Article 16 This Interpretation shall come into force on December 1, 2024. The Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Criminal Cases of Refusing to Execute Judgments or Rulings (Fa Shi [2015] No. 16) shall be abolished simultaneously. Where any judicial interpretation or normative document previously issued by the Supreme People's Court or the Supreme People's Procuratorate is inconsistent with this Interpretation, this Interpretation shall prevail.
